title: Greek myths

explain.say: Today we learn about Greek myths and gods. We will learn about Zeus and the Olympians.
Zeus was the king of the gods on Mount Olympus. He held a powerful thunderbolt weapon. He ruled over the sky and the gods.
Next, we learn about Pandora, a woman given a jar. She opened it by curiosity. Evil and suffering flew out.
We also learn about heroes like Hercules. He was famous for his amazing strength. He completed twelve difficult labors.
In real life, we see myths in stories and art. They teach us about human feelings and actions. They explain big ideas.
A common mistake is thinking all gods were always good. Myths show that even powerful gods made mistakes. They learned from their errors.

faq.q: Who was the most powerful god in Greek myth?
faq.a: Zeus was considered the king of the gods. He controlled the sky and the thunderbolt.

faq.q: What was the main thing Pandora released?
faq.a: Pandora released many evils and sufferings from the jar. Hope was the one thing left inside.
asks: What came out of the box?

faq.a: No, Hercules also showed great strength by completing twelve difficult labors. These labors tested his might.

faq.q: Are the myths true historical events?
faq.a: No, they are stories passed down through time. They teach lessons about human nature and culture.

faq.q: What is the difference between a myth and history?
faq.a: History records what is believed to have happened. Myths are stories used to explain natural things or culture.
asks: How are myths different from facts?

facts: Zeus was the ruler of the Olympian gods.
Pandora opened a jar, releasing suffering.

quiz.say: Who was the king of the gods on Mount Olympus?
quiz.why: Zeus is specifically named as the king of the gods in the myths.

wrong.0: Athena was a wise goddess, but Zeus held the title of king.
wrong.2: Poseidon was the god of the sea, not the king of all gods.
wrong.3: Hercules was a hero, not a god ruling the Olympians.

quiz.why: The story states that evils and suffering flew out when the jar was opened.

wrong.0: Curiosity was the action, not what was released by the jar.
wrong.1: The myth clearly describes things escaping the jar.
wrong.3: This is too narrow; the myths mention many forms of suffering.

quiz.say: If a hero completed twelve difficult labors, which hero was it?
quiz.why: The myths specifically credit Hercules with completing the twelve labors.

wrong.0: Odysseus is known for his clever journeys, not twelve labors.
wrong.1: Jason was known for seeking a golden fleece, not the twelve labors.
wrong.3: Achilles was a famous warrior, but the twelve labors belong to Hercules.
